messages:
ashley: Heads up — several GPU training jobs just started failing with intermittent egress timeouts during dataset download. Seen on two clusters after a node scale-up. Error in pod logs: "dial tcp: i/o timeout" when pulling model shards from our S3 bucket.

raj: Oof. Any change in node userdata / bootstrapping? Or new security group rules?

ashley: No infra rollout AFAIK. We did autoscale the GPU ASG earlier and jobs queued up. Logs show repeated TCP connection attempts then RST. kubectl describe shows Pod Running but crashlooping on data fetch.

kevin: Can you paste the `kubectl logs` snippet and `kubectl get pods -o wide`? Also which egress path (S3 via NAT or S3 gateway endpoint)?

ashley: Pasted snippet: ```Fetching shard 12/120... failed: dial tcp 52.216.12.34:443: i/o timeout``` Pod IPs are in private subnets that go out via a NAT GW in eu-west-1a. We don't have an S3 gateway endpoint in that VPC.

oncall-bot: Alert: NAT GW Connection Errors spike in eu-west-1a — 5xx count > 200 in last 5m.

marta: NAT port exhaustion is my first thought. GPU nodes spin up many worker processes, each opening parallel connections to S3. If ephemeral ports on NAT are saturated, new connections fail. Can we check NAT ActiveConnections and allocated ENIs?

kevin: Running `aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --nat-gateway-ids <id>` — NAT shows high ConnectionTrackingCount, almost hitting limit for the gateway's ports. Also noticed lots of ephemeral outbound ports tied to a handful of node ENIs.

raj: Another possibility is that interface endpoints / privatelink for internal services are misrouted and falling back to NAT, doubling load. Any interface endpoints recently updated?

ashley: We rolled out a change to the model-hosting interface endpoint earlier this morning to a new security group. But that shouldn't affect S3. However, some agents still try to hit HEADS model-hosting on privatelink which returns 502 and then fallback to external mirror over NAT — maybe causing extra retries.

kevin: Two practical fixes: 1) add an S3 gateway endpoint to the VPC so data pulls avoid NAT entirely, 2) scale NAT by adding additional NAT gateways in other AZs or move to NAT fleet with EIP pool. Immediate mitigation: reduce concurrent download threads per worker.

marta: For short-term: lowering per-process concurrency by setting ENV `MAX_S3_CONNECTIONS=8` on the training job worked for a replicate on staging — downloads resumed. For long-term: add S3 gateway endpoint + enable prefix-list -> route table so S3 traffic never hits NAT.

raj: Also check source/dest check on ENIs of the GPU nodes, but that seems unrelated. We should also audit security groups on the interface endpoint for model-hosting — if it rejects, we get retries to external host.

ashley: After lowering concurrency, two failing jobs recovered. I'll open infra ticket to provision S3 gateway and extra NAT capacity. Assign to kevin for NAT config and to infra-sre for endpoint SG audit. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll provision S3 gateway this afternoon (route table update + test). If we want to avoid cross-AZ single point, I'll propose creating NAT GW per AZ or using a managed NAT fleet.

marta: Add note for runbooks: for GPU-heavy bursts, set lower default parallelism and recommend S3 endpoint in template. I'll update docs.

ashley: Filing ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-8721 — summary: "S3 gateway + NAT capacity for GPU training bursts". Linking logs in ticket.

raj: Great. Reassigning oncall for overnight monitoring. I'll keep the thread updated if anything else pops up.
